simple.meaning: לַהֲקָה (lahăqâh) is a Hebrew concept word meaning “an assembly.” BibleIQ follows how Scripture develops this idea across its occurrences.
simple.biblicalBackground: The concept appears 1 time across 1 Samuel, beginning at 1 Samuel 19:20. Its contexts include prophetic witness.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to לַהֲקָה (H3862).
simple.whyItMatters: Concept words shape biblical themes. BibleIQ keeps the concept grounded in actual verse evidence instead of starting with a later theological definition.
simple.summary: לַהֲקָה (lahăqâh) / H3862 is traced through 1 Samuel 19:20 as a generated source-based concept entry.

definitions.full: H3862. lahaqah [ לַהֲקָה ] noun feminine dubious; according to ᵑ7 ᵑ6 ᵐ5 Aq Symm band, company (perhaps by transposing from קְהִלָּה , compare Thes ( קַהֲלָה ) The Klo Bu; see also HPS). — הַנְּבִיאִים לַהֲקִת 1Sam 19:20 .
